answer: Give each identity a memory-hard kernel seeded by its own address: it must iteratively update a large table no shortcut compresses, and at unpredictable moments echo back entries at random offsets within seconds. One honest agent runs one kernel at full memory bandwidth. A sybil operator running twenty clones on one box forces them to share the same copper traces and cache, so every clone slows, its echoes arrive late, and earnings collapse; scaling clones means buying genuinely separate machines per identity, erasing the profit.
